overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by serially deliberating, through four members' private conversations, about modifying its own vote outside a posted meeting; the single-liaison meeting itself was not a violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated outside a properly posted meeting on November 27, 2013, about reducing its Splitsville liaison delegation from two members to one.
allegations.key_passage: By a series of independent and serial conversations, four members of the Board communicated among themselves about how to modify an action of the Board taken the previous night.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Board members to review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law training video on deliberations.
Board to certify in writing to the Division of Open Government within thirty days of receipt of the letter that it has complied with the order.
